title: Calibration Protocol for Plate Reader Fluorescence
author: Geoff Baldwin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6zrhf56
materials: You have now completed this calibration protocol

steps.title: Spin down fluorescein kit tube
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the fluorescein kit tube until the pellet is firmly at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Prepare 10X fluorescein stock
steps.instruction: Resuspend fluorescein powder in 1 mL of 1X PBS to obtain a 10X stock (100 µM). After resuspension, pipette up and down and inspect the tip; continue mixing until no visible particulates remain. Skip this step if performing an RFP calibration and proceed to the alternative dye instructions.

steps.title: Dilute stock to 1X working solution
steps.instruction: Dilute the 10X stock with 1X PBS to a 1X working solution of 10 µM (e.g., add 100 µL of 10X fluorescein stock to 900 µL 1X PBS). If using Rhodamine B, dilute to a final concentration of 50 µM instead of 10 µM, then continue the protocol as written.

steps.title: Set up plate with reference and PBS
steps.instruction: Add the 1X reference working solution to all wells in column 1. Fill columns 2‑12 with an equal volume of 1X PBS (column 12 will contain PBS only). This establishes the basis for serial dilutions across columns 1‑11.

steps.title: Add PBS to wells A2–D12
steps.instruction: Dispense 100 µL of 1X PBS into wells A2, B2, C2, D2 through A12, B12, C12, D12.

steps.title: Add fluorescein to wells A1–D1
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of the 1X fluorescein stock solution to wells A1, B1, C1, and D1.

steps.title: Perform serial dilution across row A
steps.instruction: Starting with well A1, transfer 100 µL to the next well, mix by pipetting up‑and‑down three times, and repeat the transfer‑mix cycle down the row until well A11. Discard the 100 µL taken from A11 into liquid waste. Do not continue the dilution into column 12.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL from A1 to A2; mix A2 (3× up‑and‑down).
Transfer 100 µL from A2 to A3; mix A3 (3× up‑and‑down).
Continue this pattern through A10 → A11.
Discard 100 µL from A11 into waste.

steps.title: Repeat dilution for rows B–D
steps.instruction: Perform the same serial‑dilution procedure described for row A on rows B, C, and D, using the corresponding wells (B1‑B11, C1‑C11, D1‑D11).

steps.title: Measure fluorescence on plate reader
steps.instruction: Read the fluorescence of all wells using the plate reader. Ensure any automatic gain setting is turned off. If the data will be combined with an OD‑600 calibration, use identical instrument settings for both protocols.

steps.title: Record data and instrument settings
steps.instruction: Log the fluorescence values in a notebook, noting the gain (or lack thereof) used for the measurement. The standard curve remains valid even if a few wells saturate the detector.

steps.title: Import data into Excel template
steps.instruction: Open the provided iGEM Excel sheet (Fluorescence Standard Curve tab) and import the recorded data into the appropriate fields.

steps.title: Adjust settings for RFP calibration (if needed)
steps.instruction: If calibrating for a red fluorescent protein, adjust the plate reader excitation/emission wavelengths accordingly, turn off automatic gain, and consider measuring OD at 660 nm instead of 600 nm to avoid interference from protein absorbance.

steps.title: Prepare alternative dye stocks (if needed)
steps.instruction: For Texas Red, make a 100 µM stock in PBS and continue from step 4. For Rhodamine B, prepare a 50 µM stock in PBS and then follow the protocol normally.
